applies_why: The judge text resolves a challenge pressed with Luke 2:48-49 by comparing the two verses' phrases rather than weighing chain against chain by footing.
quote: Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "never verse by verse": (1) it forbids resolving a chain collision by comparing individual verses or phrases, as the judge did; (2) it only forbids demanding one isolated verse state the contrary, allowing contextual qualification as part of chain footing.
why: The judge declared the challenge underdetermined because one verse's phrase is qualified by the next verse, a verse-by-verse resolution rather than weighing the pressed chain against the defender's chain by footing.
